desc: Administering and overseeing the terms and policies associated with licensing the IT intellectual property. Create and manage the policies and terms governing the possible granting of a license to any external agent. Demarcate a clear framework that governs the licensing of any patents or copyrights held by the organization.
notes: The managed services engine - NOC, service desk, infrastructure operations.

name: Provide IT infrastructure service and capabilities
desc: Providing all the infrastructure services and capabilities required for operational activities within the IT function supporting overall business objectives.
notes: The managed services engine - NOC, service desk, infrastructure operations.

name: Operate IT user support
desc: Managing systematic user support functionality and capability through defined procedures. Determine, record, and monitor user requests. Execute issue/request resolution. Utilize escalation path when needed. Resolve issue/request.
notes: End-user support - overlaps 6.2; pick one system of record and cross-reference.

name: Triage IT issues/requests
desc: Evaluate and assign IT issues/requests accordingly to allow for the correct routing of IT issues to the relevant support teams.
notes: End-user support - overlaps 6.2; pick one system of record and cross-reference.

name: Provide IT resolution capabilities
desc: Providing the necessary skills and competencies required to efficiently provide IT resolution through the support structure.
notes: End-user support - overlaps 6.2; pick one system of record and cross-reference.

name: Manage IT user requests
desc: Creating an effective plan and structure to address and resolve requests of IT users. Determine, record, and monitor user requests. Obtain information about the effectiveness and performance of the user request handling process from the IT users through various means.
notes: End-user support - overlaps 6.2; pick one system of record and cross-reference.

name: Escalate IT requests
desc: Follow processes and procedures to escalate IT requests to required levels for resolution or effective decision making when necessary.
notes: End-user support - overlaps 6.2; pick one system of record and cross-reference.

name: Resolve IT issues/requests
desc: Creating a structure to resolve issues/requests of IT services using different mechanisms.
notes: End-user support - overlaps 6.2; pick one system of record and cross-reference.

name: Execute IT continuity and recovery action
desc: Successfully implement preventive measures to manage IT risk of exposure to internal and external threats. Integrating the disciplines of Emergency Response, Crisis Management, Disaster Recovery (technology continuity) and Business Continuity for IT.
notes: End-user support - overlaps 6.2; pick one system of record and cross-reference.

name: Manage Financial Resources
desc: Overseeing key back-office processes for organizations. This category includes process groups related to planning and management accounting, revenue accounting, general accounting and reporting, fixed-asset project accounting, payroll, accounts payable and expense reimbursements, treasury operations, internal controls, tax management, international funds/consolidation, and global trade services.
notes: NetSuite retired. QuickBooks Online is the financial system of record from 1/1/2027; HaloPSA feeds billing, Paylocity feeds payroll and expenses, Avalara handles sales/use tax.

name: Perform planning and management accounting
desc: Determining different stages of the planning process and accounting. Classify, determine, analyze, interpret, and communicate information to make up-to-date business decisions for better management and control functions.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Develop and manage financial resources strategy
desc: Ensuring the effective allocation, utilization, and sustainability of financial assets. Activities include analyzing internal and external financial drivers; identifying long-term funding needs; evaluating investment, capital, and liquidity requirements; and defining guiding financial principles that support enterprise objectives.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Perform planning/budgeting/forecasting
desc: Allocating funds to meet future and current financial goals. Led by the chief financial officer, have the finance function plan, budget, and forecast in order to determine and describe long and short-term financial goals.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Develop and maintain budget policies and procedures
desc: Formulating financial budgetary guidelines and strategies. Develop a framework for rules and regulations regarding budgets. Create a step-by-step process to achieve financial goals.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Prepare periodic budgets and plans
desc: Creating reports on a quarterly or annual basis for fund allocation. Create a financial statement that estimates revenues and expenses over a specific period of time. (Leverage budget methods such as cost-based and zero-based budgeting techniques, in light of the periodic targets outlined during Develop and maintain budget policies and procedures [10771].)
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Operationalize and implement plans to achieve budget
desc: Putting budgeting plans into practical use keeping within designated forecasting parameters.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Prepare periodic financial forecasts
desc: Creating estimates of the projected income and expenses required over a predetermined time frame. Develop the projections of profit and loss statements, balance sheets, and the cash flow forecast.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Perform variance analysis against forecasts and budgets
desc: Conducting a quantitative analysis between what was forecasted and budgeted and actual financial behavior.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Perform cost accounting and control
desc: Defining costs to be incurred and methods for optimum utilization. Determine the costs of products, processes, projects, etc. to compile in the financial statements, as well as to assist management in making decisions regarding planning and control. Control costs by managing and reducing business expenses.
notes: Cost accounting by BU; depends on the chart of accounts overhaul.

name: Perform inventory accounting
desc: Conducting accounting for assets, and finding reasons for changes (depreciation, obsolescence, deterioration, change in customer taste, increased demand, decreased market supply, etc.).
notes: Cost accounting by BU; depends on the chart of accounts overhaul.

name: Perform profit center accounting
desc: Determining the revenue, profits, and losses incurred by each unit within the organization that produces profit.
notes: Cost accounting by BU; depends on the chart of accounts overhaul.

name: Perform cost of sales analysis
desc: Studying expenses directly associated with product. Analyze the cost of sales, which is the cost of manufacturing products.
notes: Cost accounting by BU; depends on the chart of accounts overhaul.

name: Perform product costing
desc: Studying and finding out the relevant cost center for a product by studying every resource used in its making.
notes: Cost accounting by BU; depends on the chart of accounts overhaul.

name: Perform variance analysis
desc: Discovering the changes between forecasted and actual costing. Analyze actual and planned behavior by reviewing the amount of a variance on a trend line in order to maintain control over a business.
notes: Cost accounting by BU; depends on the chart of accounts overhaul.

name: Report on profitability
desc: Making a report about revenues generated by the organization or business unit concerned. This process requires the organization to create a report which shows how business is generating profits. Profits are the part which is left after paying all expenses directly related to the generation of the revenue, such as producing a product, and other expenses related to conducting business activities.
notes: Cost accounting by BU; depends on the chart of accounts overhaul.

name: Perform cost management
desc: Deciding which expenses can be avoided to reduce some costs and increase revenues. Plan and control the organization's budget to forecast future expenditures.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Determine key cost drivers
desc: Defining cost drivers for a particular activity.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Measure cost drivers
desc: Calculating cost drivers.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Determine critical activities
desc: Determine the activities that hinder the progress of finance activities. This requires the organization to determine those business activities carried out by the financial function of the organization and which are indispensable. This undertaking helps the organization triangulate those activities which are essential and where costs cannot be slashed.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Manage asset resource deployment and utilization
desc: Distributing or allocating asset resources in different processes for optimal utilization.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Evaluate and manage financial performance
desc: Checking and achieving predetermined financial targets and timelines. Assess and manage the profitability, feasibility, and consistency of a business or project. Study the revenues generated.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Assess customer and product profitability
desc: Studying product demand and targeted customer preferences. Study customers' demands or preferences after deducting the cost of delivering the final product.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Evaluate new products
desc: Checking demand about a specific product by a customer segment. Conduct a detailed study--or research a customer behavior or preference for a product--in order to determine its production and profitability in a specific market.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Perform life cycle costing
desc: Determining the cost of delivering an end product at different stages of production. Study the total life cycle of a product/process to determine how much revenue and production cost will be incurred at every stage in order to make strategic decisions.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Optimize customer and product mix
desc: Creating the best fit between a product and the end user. Maximize the customer base by providing different products in the market.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Track performance of new-customer and product strategies
desc: Observing the behavior of a new set of customers for different products. Prepare strategies to improve sales and profits.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Prepare activity-based performance measures
desc: Evaluating performance based on different sets of activities created by management to measure performance.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Manage continuous cost improvement
desc: Conducting activities to improve cost distribution regularly. Follow or adopt different ways of reducing costs.
notes: Budget, forecast, and BU-level profitability - the Operations seat's scorecard.

name: Perform revenue accounting
desc: Comparing revenue targets to reality. Review all transactions and entries passed in final accounts in a year in order to examine profits.

name: Process customer credit
desc: Evaluating and processing requests for advances. Evaluate credit requests by customers requiring loans to buy products/services.

name: Establish credit policies
desc: Creating guidelines for providing advances. Set up credit standards, credit terms, and collection policies.

name: Analyze/Approve new account applications
desc: Checking and accepting new requests based on eligibility criteria. Analyze the status of applicants and requirements to be met for a new account.

name: Analyze credit scoring history
desc: Reviewing past credit scores to determine the if a line of credit will be extended to potential customers. This could also include extending additional credit to existing accounts.

name: Forecast credit scoring requirement
desc: Planning credit score requirements based on established credit policies.

name: Review existing accounts
desc: Evaluating existing account holders and their past performance. Regularly review existing accounts to get the required information about the status at present.

name: Produce credit/collection reports
desc: Preparing account payable reports about payments to be made according to accounting rules and principles, and providing the reports to management.

name: Reinstate or suspend accounts based on credit policies
desc: Closing or restarting accounts according to changes made in credit policies.

name: Invoice customer
desc: Preparing detailed reports of customer purchases. Prepare a commercial document between the seller and customer with details about transaction. Detail the quantity purchased, price of products/services, date, parties involved, unique invoice number, and tax information.
owner: AR Clerk (runs invoices); XO / Project Controller (approves)
notes: Recurring contract and T&M billing originates in Halo.

name: Maintain customer/product master files
desc: Creating and updating a record of customers and the products being purchased by them in a database. This process element requires the organization to maintain a database of customers and their purchases. Such a master-file can be used to ensure customer touch point, enhance customer satisfaction, explore cross selling opportunities, and identify future trends. This database will include several particulars about the personal details of the organization's customers and a tracking of the products being sold.
notes: Recurring contract and T&M billing originates in Halo.

name: Generate customer billing data
desc: Preparing detailed reports about products purchased by customers. Record and generate a detail account of transactions made by customers fat a particular time and location. Include all details about products such as price, quantity, and name.
notes: Recurring contract and T&M billing originates in Halo.

name: Transmit billing data to customers
desc: Providing information to customers about purchases made by them. Communicate the details of purchases. Provide customers with a copy of details for their reference.
notes: Recurring contract and T&M billing originates in Halo.

name: Post receivable entries
desc: Registering transactions and their scheduled payments.
notes: Recurring contract and T&M billing originates in Halo.

name: Resolve customer billing inquiries
desc: Checking and solving billing queries raised by customers.
notes: Recurring contract and T&M billing originates in Halo.

name: Process accounts receivable (AR)
desc: Processing payments due from customers. This includes all processing of funds received, whether by check or electronically. This does not include the generation of invoices.

name: Establish AR policies
desc: Creating rules and regulations to be followed in case of credit sales to customers. Create rules and procedures to follow at the time of sale (e.g., the allowable number of installments).

name: Receive/Deposit customer payments
desc: Collecting cash from customers. Deposit it into bank account. Make entries into the books of accounts.

name: Apply cash remittances
desc: Checking and moving funds between countries for business activities, typically through authorized remittance agents.

name: Prepare AR reports
desc: Preparing reports that detail balances due or what to collect from customers at a certain point in time.

name: Post AR activity to the general ledger
desc: Preparing the general ledger for account receivables from journals. Place all journal entries related to accounts receivables in the general ledger accounts of a business.

name: Manage and process collections
desc: Posting entries to respective accounts, and preparing accounts for receivables. Manage the cash collected by the business from its debtors. Record it in the books of accounts to provide clear information about the availability of the cash.

name: Establish policies for delinquent accounts
desc: Creating a process to follow in case of a failed payment by account holders. Create rules and regulations for the account holder who has failed to make at least the minimum monthly payment by the due date.

name: Analyze delinquent account balances
desc: Examining balance statements of accountholders who failed to make required payments. Study or review the account details of customers' past payments when preparing negotiations policies.

name: Correspond/Negotiate with delinquent accounts
desc: Determine ways for customers in default to repay debts (e.g., allowing more time or discounts).

name: Discuss account resolution with internal parties
desc: Determining rules for handling accounts. Discuss and plan with internal parties (department heads, managers, and senior management) about rules to follow in coming months.

name: Process adjustments/write off balances
desc: Maintaining reserves for write-offs and adjustments. Adjust or write off certain expenses and losses.

name: Perform recovery workout
desc: Renegotiating the terms of a loan agreement in order to recoup money from a default account.

name: Manage default accounts
desc: Managing accounts that have not met the requirements agreed upon to pay off outstanding debts.

name: Manage and process adjustments/deductions
desc: Creating and providing funds for necessary adjustments and deductions, including all expenses that were required for the business at certain point in time.

name: Establish policies/procedures for adjustments
desc: Creating guidelines to follow in case of adjustments to business processes.

name: Analyze adjustments
desc: Checking changes made in accounts during the year. Examine the alterations made in final accounts to rectify errors/omissions.

name: Correspond/Negotiate with customer
desc: Providing suitable offers to customers. Present different offers (e.g., discounts) available for customers or buyers.

name: Discuss resolution with internal parties
desc: Discussing and planning with internal parties (department heads, managers, and senior management) about rules to follow in coming months.

name: Prepare chargeback invoices
desc: Creating a mechanism for consumer protection in case of a higher price charged. When a supplier sells a product at a higher price to the distributor than the price they have set with the end user, submit a chargeback to the supplier to recover the money lost in the transaction.

name: Process related entries
desc: Recording business transactions as they occur in order to provide a balanced accounts for financial reporting.

name: Perform general accounting and reporting
desc: Making statements about business activities and functions. Prepare financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, statement of cash flows, and statement of stockholders' equity) according to accounting concepts and principles.

name: Manage financial policies and procedures
desc: Creating procedures to perform general accounting and reporting. Follow the rules and regulations made for a particular process in the business. Publish accounting policies.

name: Negotiate service-level agreements
desc: Agreeing upon terms and conditions. Negotiate an agreement between two or more parties, the customer and service providers. Specify scope, quality, and responsibilities.

name: Establish accounting policies
desc: Establishing policies and procedures to prepare financial statements, including methods, measurement systems, and procedures for providing disclosures.

name: Publish accounting policies
desc: Creating a written copy of agreed-upon procedures for preparing financial statements, and making them available to the public.

name: Set and enforce approval limits
desc: Implementing parameters for accounting. Apply set conditions for any approval process.

name: Establish common financial systems
desc: Establishing processes and procedures to exercise financial control and accountability. Record, verify, and report transactions that affect revenues, expenditures, assets, and liabilities.

name: Perform general accounting
desc: Applying basic principles, concepts, and accounting practices in recording and preparing final accounts, and using accounting information in management.

name: Maintain chart of accounts
desc: Preparing trial balance account from general ledgers. List all accounts used in the general ledger. Alter accounts according to business requirements.

name: Process journal entries
desc: Making ledger and trial balance accounts from journal entries. This process requires the organization to record every transaction into accounts done by business. It is a base documents for preparing final accounts of company.

name: Process allocations
desc: Allocating funds across functions. Apportion funds in line with the budgets created. Formalize allocations in centralized internal records.

name: Process period end adjustments
desc: Updating journal entries to adjust the balance of income and expenses at the end of an accounting period.

name: Post and reconcile intercompany transactions
desc: Checking accounts separately for a parent and subsidiary company. Manage relationship between a parent company and subsidiaries. Document intercompany transactions in separate financial statements.

name: Reconcile general ledger accounts
desc: Reviewing general ledger accounts for a parent and subsidiaries companies. Validate the integrity of account balances on the company's general ledger of accounts. Review and compare general ledger accounts balances with source documents to ensure that balances match.

name: Perform consolidations and process eliminations
desc: Aggregating different processes in the business. Eliminate discontinued processes.

name: Prepare trial balance
desc: Balancing debit and credit balances of trial balance to preparing final accounts. Calculate the total debits and credits in company's accounts. Correspond the sum of all debits with the sum of all credits. Adjust entries as appropriate.

name: Prepare and post management adjustments
desc: Accounting for changes due to country-level policy changes. Record adjustments made by management in the accounts.

name: Perform fixed-asset accounting
desc: Accounting for long-term and fixed assets. Record purchased, fixed assets that are not easily convertible into cash. Account for costs, useful life, resale value, depreciation, and amortization.

name: Establish fixed-asset policies and procedures
desc: Creating rules for fixed assets market valuation. Make rules and regulations for fixed assets regarding depreciation, provisions, resale, usage, etc.

name: Maintain fixed-asset master data files
desc: Keeping reports up-to-date regarding fixed assets. Create a fixed assets database detailing price, life cycle, depreciation rate, resale value, installation information, usage information, etc.

name: Process and record fixed-asset additions and retires
desc: Keeping a summary of sales and purchases of assets. Record any expenses made for new assets purchased and sales of any old assets during the fiscal year.

name: Process and record fixed-asset adjustments, enhancements, revaluations, and transfers
desc: Keeping a summary of expenses for installing and modifying assets. Record any expenses made for new assets purchased, any expenses incurred on improvements, the valuation of assets to reach current market price, and any transfer assets from one location to another during the fiscal year.

name: Process and record fixed-asset maintenance and repair expenses
desc: Maintaining a record of expenses necessitated for repairs and the preservation of assets. Administer and oversee the maintenance and repair of any fixed assets. Record all related transactions.

name: Calculate and record depreciation expense
desc: Carrying out accounting for depreciation over fixed assets. Compute the sums necessitated. Maintain a record of the cost value of fixed assets over their useful life in the book of accounts.

name: Reconcile fixed-asset ledger
desc: Balancing the ledger account balance for fixed assets. Correct errors in the books of fixed assets. Provide correct information in relevant accounts.

name: Track fixed-assets including physical inventory
desc: Checking and updating the record of all raw materials and fixed assets. Track all fixes asset. Maintain a record of all inventory items.

name: Provide fixed-asset data to support tax, statutory, and regulatory reporting
desc: Showing market value and related expenses on fixed assets data for taxation. Provide complete information recorded in the books of fixed assets about purchase price, depreciation, installation charges, resale market value etc. for tax and regulatory purposes.

name: Perform financial reporting
desc: Reporting on the organization's financial status to stakeholders. Include balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, and statements of shareholders' equity.

name: Prepare business unit financial statements
desc: Making reports of subsidiaries units to show profits generated from them. Prepare financial statements (balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements and statements of shareholders' equity) for a single unit of a business.

name: Prepare consolidated financial statements
desc: Making final accounts for all units of company together. Prepare combined financial statements of a parent company and its subsidiaries (i.e., separate legal entities controlled by a parent company) showing assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses, and cash flows.

name: Perform business unit reporting/review management reports
desc: Making reports for units/subsidiaries to help management in decision making. Prepare financial statements (balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, and statements of shareholders' equity) for a single unit of a business. Break down profits and losses by function/unit, clients, products, and region.

name: Perform consolidated reporting/review of cost management reports
desc: Making reports for all units to help higher management in decision making. Prepare combined financial statements of a parent company and its all subsidiaries (separate legal entities controlled by a parent company) showing assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses and cash flows, and also going through periodic reports which shows the actual and estimated costs and their variances.

name: Prepare statements for board review
desc: Preparing a draft of financial statements for the board to review before they are sent to the auditor.

name: Produce quarterly/annual filings and shareholder reports
desc: Making and presenting financial reports to stakeholders. Create annual and quarterly financial statements for reporting purposes. Prepare shareholder reports with details of the profit-and-loss account, balance sheet, and past year's business activities.

name: Produce regulatory reports
desc: Reporting raw or summary data for final accounts following rules and regulations.

name: Perform legal and management consolidation
desc: Carrying out activities associated with legal and management consolidation. Legal consolidation can include currency conversion, balance carry forward, and consolidation of journal entries. Management consolidation can include reporting on financials on a reporting cycle basis to gauge the performance of the organization.

name: Manage fixed-asset project accounting
desc: Managing accounts for large funds-invested projects. Manage and account for fixed assets projects (capital projects), which required significant capital investments over many years.

name: Perform capital planning and project approval
desc: Preparing a project finance report to solicit approvals in capital projects. Prepare budgets for projects that require heavy investments. Report on project finances to solicit approvals from management.

name: Develop capital investment policies and procedures
desc: Creating procedures and policies to follow for investing in capital projects. Create rules and regulations regarding large investment plans, which require in-depth forecasting for expenditure and revenue.

name: Develop and approve capital expenditure plans and budgets
desc: Creating budgets, and soliciting approvals for capital projects. Prepare budgets for projects that require heavy investments. Secure approvals from management.

name: Review and approve capital projects and fixed-asset acquisitions
desc: Evaluating and supporting capital investments in projects and fixed assets. Confirm details of capital projects. Secure approvals from managements for large investments.

name: Conduct financial justification for project approval
desc: Reviewing all project business cases in order to substantiate projected financial gains. Validate any project's business case. Juxtapose the benefits derived from moving a project forward against the associated costs.

name: Perform capital project accounting
desc: Accounting for large-scale and large-cost investments. Manage and account for ongoing activities related to capital projects, including setting up new projects, recording project transactions, monitoring and tracking spending, closing and capitalizing projects, and measuring the financial returns on completed projects.

name: Create project account codes
desc: Giving reference codes for every project.

name: Record project-related transactions
desc: Noting every transaction during a project in a common financial database. Document all transactions associated with any project. Maintain a centralized repository of all such financial data.

name: Monitor and track capital projects and budget spending
desc: Evaluating project progress and funds invested. Observe and track significant funds invested on any long-term project. Compare to budget.

name: Close/Capitalize projects
desc: Checking for returns generated from projects for decision making. Evaluate capital projects that require heavy investments. Decide whether to proceed based on the revenues generated.

name: Measure financial returns on completed capital projects
desc: Comparing a finished project's profitability with forecasted returns. Scrutinize revenues generated by completed projects that required heavy investments. Determine profitability.

name: Process payroll
desc: Handling reporting time, managing pay, and processing taxes from salaries. Pay employees. Withhold taxes. Confirm the correct funds are paid to the correct government agency.

name: Report time
desc: Recording the reporting time of employees on-site. Track working days, salary calculations, holidays taken, number of hours spend in the office, billing hours, etc.

name: Establish policies and procedures
desc: Developing policies and procedures for the HR function to calculate compensation.

name: Collect and record employee time worked
desc: Tracking billing hours of each employee on daily basis.

name: Analyze and report paid and unpaid leave
desc: Tracking leaves allowed and taken by employees.

name: Monitor regular, overtime, and other hours
desc: Observing the number of hours worked by an employees on daily basis. Track the number of hours worked by an employee, as well as the number of hours worked beyond normal working hour's according to company standards.

name: Analyze and report employee utilization
desc: Monitoring the number of productive hours for employees.

name: Manage pay
desc: Managing the total payments made in employees payroll, including bonuses and compensation.

name: Enter employee time worked into payroll system
desc: Tracking the number of hours worked for the payroll system. Register the number of hours worked by an employee into the payroll system for the purpose of calculating salaries or wages.

name: Maintain and administer employee earnings information
desc: Tracking and oversee salary breakups of employees. This process requires the organization to manage and update information pertaining to the structure of every employee's salary. This would involve the updating any changes to the salary structures of the employees, in a central repository which can be accessed by pertinent departments.

name: Maintain and administer applicable deductions
desc: Processing salary deductions for tax purposes. Keep and manage the details of every employee's salary deductions based on their expenses and investments during the year.

name: Monitor changes in tax status of employees
desc: Tracking changes in the salary structure of employees for tax deductions.

name: Process and distribute payments
desc: Processing and distributing salaries to all employees. Execute the payroll management function through the dispensation of employee salaries. Leverage a centralized database of all payroll expenses.

name: Process and distribute manual checks
desc: Handling incorrect/omitted salary payments.

name: Process period-end adjustments
desc: Adjusting salary deductions for tax purposes at the end of the year.

name: Respond to employee payroll inquiries
desc: Addressing salary-related queries raised by employees.

name: Manage and process payroll taxes
desc: Deducting and paying taxes from employees' salaries.

name: Develop tax plan
desc: Devising a method to minimize payroll tax liability by means of allowances, deductions, exclusions or exemptions.

name: Manage tax plan
desc: Overseeing maintaining the reduction of payroll taxes [14075].

name: Calculate and pay applicable payroll taxes
desc: Paying tax according to appropriate deductions made from salaries. Calculate and pay the tax liabilities according to the salaries and tax regulations of employees with the help of certified chartered accountants.

name: Produce and distribute employee annual tax statements
desc: Providing tax deductions statements created by certified chartered accountants to every employee for their reference or refunds.

name: File regulatory payroll tax forms
desc: Filling taxes, and highlighting different sources of income and expenditures made.

name: Process accounts payable and expense reimbursements
desc: Handling bills and reimbursements to be made. Make payments for goods or services taken or used on behalf of the organization.

name: Process accounts payable (AP)
desc: Processing payments of operating expenses and other supplier charges. This includes the development of policies and procedures around processing of accounts payable and all operations. This process is often supported by key technology enablers.

name: Verify AP pay file with purchase order vendor master file
desc: Matching records of bills to be paid with accounts. Check accounts payable entries with vendor's account for every payment made.

name: Maintain/Manage electronic commerce
desc: Tracking all online transactions.

name: Audit invoices and key data in AP system
desc: Monitoring and evaluating bills registered in accounts books. Check all invoices. Maintain records.

name: Approve payments
desc: Processing payments for products/services.

name: Process financial accruals and reversals
desc: Handling transactions for accruals and reversals. Record transactions in the books of accounts on an accrual basis (irrespective of the actual cash flow) and reversals basis (cancel out the adjusting entries) for balancing accounts.

name: Process payables taxes
desc: Filing the amount of taxes that a company owes as of the balance sheet date. Prepare tax returns, including the income tax filing for an individual or business entity from earnings.

name: Research/Resolve payable exceptions
desc: Resolving any atypical or inconsistent situation concerning payments to be made by the organization. Address any exceptional case of accounts payable on an ad hoc basis, by seeking counsel or carrying out any necessary research.

name: Process payments
desc: Making payments for products/services on due dates (payment cycle) decided by parties involved.

name: Respond to AP inquiries
desc: Clarifying or address queries relating to the particulars of AP such as date, discounts, amount, and installments. Coordinate with concerned parties about the fulfillment of bills payable.

name: Retain records
desc: Keeping bills of every transaction for future reference.

name: Adjust accounting records
desc: Rectifying for alterations occurred in accounts while recording.

name: Process expense reimbursements
desc: Processing reimbursements to employees for the expenses incurred during the course of business. Approve and process advancements and reimbursements for employee expenses on the organization's behalf. Capture and report relevant tax data and manage personal accounts.

name: Establish and communicate expense reimbursement policies and approval limits
desc: Explaining policies and procedures related to reimbursements requests by employees. Set policies regarding reimbursement process and amount limits etc. Inform employees.

name: Capture and report relevant tax data
desc: Collecting and reporting all pertinent information regarding the taxes paid by the organization's employees.

name: Approve reimbursements and advances
desc: Permitting expense reimbursement requests from employees.

name: Process reimbursements and advances
desc: Paying for expense reimbursement requests from employees. (Follow Approve reimbursements and advances [10882] according to policies and conditions.)

name: Manage personnel accounts
desc: Maintaining accounts of individuals who are connected with business.

name: Manage corporate credit cards
desc: Handling and authoring credit cards to business entities or for corporate purchases.

name: Establish corporate credit card policies and approval limits
desc: Developing procedures for using company credit cards. Set or approve credit limits.

name: Process corporate credit card requests
desc: Handling applications credit card applications for business expenses.

name: Order corporate credit cards
desc: Obtaining credit cards for business-related expenses.

name: Manage corporate credit card accounts
desc: Handling credit card accounts of business customers.

name: Approve/Change credit limits
desc: Authorizing changes to the available credit advances.

name: Cancel/Deactivate credit card
desc: Blocking an existing credit card to disable all future transactions.

name: Manage treasury operations
desc: Managing business's investments in trading in bonds, currencies, financial derivatives, etc. Manage the financial assets and holdings of the organization. Optimize the organization's liquidity. Invest excess cash. Reduce financial risks.

name: Manage treasury policies and procedures
desc: Managing rules and regulations for investments in trading in bonds, currencies, financial derivatives, etc. Establish policies and procedures for investments made. Optimize liquidity in treasury operations.

name: Establish scope and governance of treasury operations
desc: Selecting opportunities and the authoritative body for investments in trading in bonds, currencies, financial derivatives, etc.

name: Establish and publish treasury policies
desc: Creating and providing investment regulations for the organization. Establish policies and procedures for investments to optimize liquidity in treasury operations. Create a written copy of it.

name: Develop treasury procedures
desc: Making processes for investing. Create steps for investments in bonds, currencies, and financial derivatives in order to optimize company's liquidity, invest excess cash, and reduce its financial risks.

name: Monitor treasury procedures
desc: Checking treasury processes in order to optimize company's liquidity, invest excess cash, and reduce its financial risks.

name: Audit treasury procedures
desc: Auditing the treasury function.

name: Revise treasury procedures
desc: Reassessing all treasury procedures based on audit findings.

name: Develop and confirm internal controls for treasury
desc: Creating and managing the internal control systems for investments in bonds, currencies, and financial derivatives to verify procedures.

name: Define treasury security requirements
desc: Describing the need of treasury security requirements for controlling access, reliability of information, accountability, and availability of information in the organization.

name: Manage cash
desc: Taking care of all cash-related activities in the business. Manage and reconcile cash positions. Manage cash equivalents. Process and oversee electronic fund transfers. Develop cash flow forecasts. Manage cash flows. Produce cash management accounting transactions and reports. Manage and oversee banking relationships. Analyze, negotiate, resolve, and confirm bank fees.

name: Manage and reconcile cash positions
desc: Correcting cash differences in the books of accounts. Make optimum utilization of funds available in the business. Check for differences to rectify.

name: Manage cash equivalents
desc: Taking care of all cash-related activities in the business. Utilize short-term assets that can be easily convertible into cash, such as marketable securities, commercial paper and short-term government bonds, and treasury bills.

name: Process and oversee electronic fund transfers (EFTs)
desc: Supervising all online transactions.

name: Develop cash flow forecasts
desc: Preparing forecasts for the cash generated or used by the organization.

name: Manage cash flows
desc: Delaying the outflow of funds as long as possible, but encourage the inflow of as fast as possible.

name: Produce cash management accounting transactions and reports
desc: Presenting reports on all cash-related activities. Collect and manage short-term investing activities. Prepare reports of all transactions done.

name: Manage and oversee banking relationships
desc: Maintaining and directing the course of relationships with banking partners.

name: Analyze, negotiate, resolve, and confirm bank fees
desc: Studying and finalizing bank fees for services provided by banks. Negotiate and finalize nominal fees that bank charges for various services, such as requesting a deposit slip or counter check or certifying papers.

name: Manage in-house bank accounts
desc: Managing financial services provided by an in-house bank structure in the corporation that is operating like a commercial bank.

name: Manage in-house bank accounts for subsidiaries
desc: Maintaining subsidiaries' company accounts opened with bank inside the corporation. Manage different financial services provided by in-house bank structure for parent companies' subsidiaries or branches.

name: Manage and facilitate inter-company borrowing transactions
desc: Arranging loans for subsidiaries from in-house banks.

name: Manage centralized outgoing payments on behalf of subsidiaries
desc: Handling payments made for subsidiaries by parent company.

name: Manage central incoming payments on behalf of subsidiaries
desc: Handling payments received by parent company for subsidiaries.

name: Manage internal payments and netting transactions
desc: Taking care of all business outflows and recording as whole. Manage making all payments for the organization and its units or subsidiaries. Track in books of accounts of parent company.

name: Calculate interest and fees for in-house bank accounts
desc: Computing all expenses paid to and receivables collected over the organization's banking activity. Calculate all charges and receivables, towards interest, fees, and any other payments over its own bank accounts. Record transactions in the books of accounts.

name: Provide account statements for in-house bank accounts
desc: Facilitating account statements for all in-house banking activity.

name: Manage debt and investment
desc: Taking care of the organization's financial position. Manage its loans or debts from different sources and investments. Leverage the most profitable options to balance the financial position in the market.

name: Establish investment policy
desc: Developing and instituting principles that the organization ill use in making investments.

name: Manage financial intermediary relationships
desc: Maintaining smooth relations with financial investment banks that help availing loans and services.

name: Manage liquidity
desc: Managing and maintaining enough liquidity in form of cash and cash equivalents in the business to meet urgent and timely requirements

name: Manage issuer exposure
desc: Managing the exposure incurred by the issuer for providing credit to the borrower.

name: Process and oversee debt and investment transactions
desc: Tracking loans taken and money invested in different options. Arrange and supervise loans from banks and individuals and investments in different available and profitable options.

name: Process and oversee foreign currency transactions
desc: Arranging and supervising foreign exchange rate changes to avoid loss on foreign-currency transactions.

name: Produce debt and investment accounting transaction reports
desc: Creating transactions report of loans and investments. Prepare and maintain records of loans and investment transactions.

name: Process and oversee interest rate transactions
desc: Supervising the interest paid or received by the organization. Arrange and supervise interest rate swap transactions to manage exposure to fluctuations in interest rates. Or attain a marginally lower rate of interest than could be gained through a swap.

name: Monitor and execute risk and hedging transactions
desc: Performing transactions that limit investment risk with the help of derivatives, such as options and futures contracts. Manage interest rates, foreign exchange, and exposure risks. Develop and execute hedging transactions. Evaluate and refine hedging positions. Produce hedge accounting transactions and reports. Monitor credit.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Develop risk management/hedging strategy
desc: Taking an investment position to offset exposure to certain risks. This may include purchasing opposite of the organization's position in the marketplace, using derivatives transactions, or futures contracts.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage interest rate risk
desc: Handling risks arising from changes in the interest rate.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage interest rate market data
desc: Collecting and storing data that pertains to interest rate markets.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Determine interest rate exposure for all markets
desc: Identifying potential interest rate risks for all markets.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Determine interest rate hedge requirements in accordance with risk policy
desc: Deciding the requirements on interest rate investments that are made by trading in futures or options market, on the basis of the accepted risk policy.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Execute interest rate trades
desc: Performing trading on interest rates.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage foreign exchange risk
desc: Taking care of foreign-exchange risks.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage foreign exchange market data
desc: Handling and processing information about changes in foreign exchange rates.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Determine foreign exchange exposure for all currencies
desc: Establishing potential foreign exchange risks for all currencies.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Determine foreign exchange hedge requirements in accordance with risk policy
desc: Deciding the requirements on investments in foreign exchange made by trading in futures or options market, on the basis of current risk policy.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Execute foreign exchange trades
desc: Executing all aspects for foreign exchange trade within foreign exchange market. This includes buying, selling, and exchanging currencies at the current or expressed price point.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage foreign exchange balance sheet risk
desc: Overseeing the foreign exchange balance sheet with an eye towards potential risk. Risks include changes in conversion rates between the time the transaction occurred and when it is completed, or when transactions are made in a denomination other than that of the organization's base currency.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage exposure risk
desc: Taking care of exposure risks. Maintain financial investments in particular investments or a portfolios that could be risky for the organization.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Determine current customer exposures and limit exceptions
desc: Establishing ongoing risks that the customers face, and the exceptions to exceeded limits.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Resolve customer exposure limit violations
desc: Settling cases that involve violations of customer exposure limit.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage customer collateral
desc: Handling customer securities to recover loans that are not paid back.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Perform annual customer credit reviews
desc: Conducting reviews to assess customer credit on a yearly basis. Introduce changes or make recommendations, if needed.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Execute hedging transactions
desc: Implementing hedging strategy in attempt to alleviate risk. This will include all options, depravities, and futures contracts agreed upon in Develop risk management/hedging strategy [12974].
notes: No hedging program.

name: Measure physical positions
desc: Evaluating investments made in some market to offset the risks of investing in a contrary or opposing market.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Establish hedges
desc: Determining which hedge options to execute.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Unwind hedges
desc: Closing out a position or cashing in derivatives early.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Evaluate and refine hedging positions
desc: Examining options in the market for hedging investments. Select an option.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Monitor credit
desc: Revising credit reports periodically for accurateness and changes that could be suggestive of duplicitous activity.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Produce hedge accounting transactions and reports
desc: Preparing and documenting accounts and records of all hedging investment transactions to reduce risks due to change in markets.
notes: No hedging program.

name: Manage financial fraud/dispute cases
desc: Handling cases that involve financial fraud. Resolve disputes.

name: Manage internal controls
desc: Administering internal controls. This process requires the organization to manage entity's board of trustees, management, and other personnel in order to offer judicious assurance about the achievement of effectiveness, proficiency of operations, and reliability of financial reporting.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Establish internal controls, policies, and procedures
desc: Forming rules and regulations to ensure the achievement of effectiveness, proficiency of operations, and reliability of financial reporting.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Establish board of directors and audit committee
desc: Establishing board of directors and auditing committee in order to assign roles and responsibilities for internal controls.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Define and communicate code of ethics
desc: Outlining and communicating a code of ethics act responsibly.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Assign roles and responsibility for internal controls
desc: Defining roles, responsibilities, and accountabilities for effectiveness and proficiency of operations and reliability of financial reporting.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Define business process objectives and risks
desc: Outlining the objectives and risks associated with a process. Delineate process goals. Determine the risks attached to it. Determine what the process is meant to accomplish, potential issues, a timeline of potential risks, the scope and potential impact of risks, etc.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Define entity/unit risk tolerances
desc: Outlining the risk tolerance levels of individual units, as well as the organization as a whole. Determine the specific maximum risk to take in quantitative terms for each relevant risk subcategory, including strategic, operational, financial, and compliance risks.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Operate controls and monitor compliance with internal controls policies and procedures
desc: Performing planning, management, operations, and monitoring of internal control mechanism policies and procedures in order to manage internal controls.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Monitor control effectiveness
desc: Overseeing the activities for internal controls. Observe the effectiveness of policies, procedures, techniques, and mechanisms actions taken to minimize risk.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Remediate control deficiencies
desc: Taking corrective measures for policies, procedures, techniques, and mechanisms actions taken to minimize risk. (Conduct in accordance with Monitor control effectiveness [10918] in order to determine and rectify the control deficiencies.)
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Report on internal controls compliance
desc: Reporting on internal controls compliance to the appropriate authority, including IT regulations and pertinent data.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Report to external auditors
desc: Reporting to external auditors. This process requires the organization to report to external auditors about the regulations for any critical data that the organization is holding.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Report to regulators, share-/debt-holders, securities exchanges, etc.
desc: Reporting to regulators, shareholders, debt holders, securities exchanges, etc. about IT regulations and pertinent data.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Report to third parties
desc: Reporting to suppliers, customers, and partners that are doing business with the company about IT regulations and pertinent data.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Report to internal management
desc: Reporting to internal management (all employees, directors, and management) about IT regulations and pertinent data.
notes: Control design and operation - the backbone of a SOC 2 readiness effort.

name: Manage taxes
desc: Estimating the organization's periodic tax liabilities. Ensure that appropriate taxing authorities receive tax return filings and payments when due.

name: Develop tax strategy and plan
desc: Setting targets for periodic tax liabilities. Assess the tax impact of various activities such as the acquisition or disposal of fixed assets or a deliberate change in number of employee.

name: Develop foreign, national, state, and local tax strategy
desc: Developing a tax strategy for foreign, national, state, local administration. Set up tax strategies for foreign trade in imports and exports and at national, state, and local level.

name: Consolidate and optimize total tax plan
desc: Combining and enhancing a rational analysis of a financial condition or plan from a tax perspective in order to align financial goals through efficient tax planning.

name: Maintain tax master data
desc: Maintaining a master file about the rational analysis of a financial condition or plan from a tax perspective in order to align financial goals through efficient tax planning.

name: Process taxes
desc: Processing the taxes of the organization in line with the regional taxation structure, including corporate, property, excise, and service taxes.

name: Perform tax planning/strategy
desc: Creating and implementing strategies for taxes to be paid or collected by the business.

name: Prepare tax returns
desc: Preparing and submitting tax reports for every employee to the tax department in order to show the tax paid and deducted from their salaries in the year.

name: Prepare foreign taxes
desc: Preparing reports about paid or accrued foreign taxes to an overseas country.

name: Calculate deferred taxes
desc: Calculating the income that has been realized when the tax on that income has not.

name: Account for taxes
desc: Managing the organization's financial accounts for the purpose of taxation. Prepare and maintain the tax paid by the organization to the country they have business in.

name: Monitor tax compliance
desc: Checking and correcting the tax policies according to the rules and regulations set by the organization.

name: Address tax inquiries
desc: Addressing any tax queries by any regulatory or government authorities. Review historical records related to taxation within the organization in order to respond to queries.

name: Manage international funds/consolidation
desc: Managing cash collections and disbursements made by operating units across the enterprise. When appropriate, transfer cash from the operating units to parent-level bank accounts managed by the organization's treasury team.
notes: Single-currency, domestic operations.

name: Monitor international rates
desc: Forecasting and monitoring changes in foreign currency value or interest rates around the world that play an important role in the organization.
notes: Single-currency, domestic operations.

name: Manage transactions
desc: Managing any transfer of funds in the course of conducting cross-border trades or investments, including conversion across currencies. Find the most suitable alternative for making payments, while saving taxes and avoiding any unwarranted regulation, with the objective of protecting capital.
notes: Single-currency, domestic operations.

name: Monitor currency exposure/hedge currency
desc: Assessing exposure to potential financial losses as a result of changes in the value of currencies. Forecast the impact of movements in foreign currency values. Enter into financial transactions designed to offset or limit potential exposure to loss.
notes: Single-currency, domestic operations.

name: Report results
desc: Documenting and reporting accounting entries to formally report financial gains or losses experienced as a result of foreign exchange activity.
notes: Single-currency, domestic operations.

name: Perform global trade services
desc: Making and collecting payments for transactions in products/services, and transporting them to interested markets.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Screen sanctioned party list
desc: Evaluating the approved list of parties for engaging in international trade in order to ensure the safety of the organization's business transactions. Examine agents that have been granted legal rights to engage in global trade and their credentials.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Control exports and imports
desc: Overseeing and directing the flow of trade to/from the organization in order to ensure financial gains.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Classify products
desc: Systematically categorizing products/services for their suitability to international trade. Create classes and categories for demarcating the types of products suitable for international trade. Study requisite national and international standards and the adherence of the organization's portfolio of offerings to these.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Perform currency conversion
desc: Identifying current exchange rates between two currencies and converting the foreign currency to that of the local monetary unit. I.E., yen to US dollar.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Calculate duty
desc: Computing the excise duty to be paid during international trade.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Communicate with customs
desc: Communicating with the customs department to ensure fluid compliance. Share pertinent information mandated by law with the government agency that controls and collects the duties levied for the international exchange of products/services.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Document trade
desc: Documenting and recording the trade processes while making transactions, noting the description, quality, number, transportation medium, indemnity, and inspection.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Process trade preferences
desc: Preparing global trade under preference, which allows the organization to import/export products at a lower or nil rate of customs duty and/or levy charge.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Handle restitution
desc: Administering and overseeing all restitution activities the organization may be subjected to. Manage compliance with apposite legal frameworks. Make any restitution that may be required by law; comply with authorities over any fines or non-financial measures imposed.
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Prepare letter of credit
desc: Creating a document assuring that a seller will receive payment when certain delivery conditions are met. (If the buyer is unable to make payment on the purchase, a bank covers the outstanding amount.)
notes: No cross-border trade.

name: Acquire, Construct, and Manage Assets
desc: Relating to the design, construction, acquisition, and management of both productive and non-productive assets.
notes: Asset-light services firm. Facilities in Baton Rouge, Houston and Birmingham; internal IT assets.

name: Plan and acquire assets
desc: Planning, acquiring, and managing facilities, workspaces, and supporting assets. Acquire, configure, and manage facilities and workspaces, to include supporting equipment and materials.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Develop property strategy and long term vision
desc: Strategizing a long-term vision for managing properties. Prepare strategies and a long-term vision for managing purchased/retained properties.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Confirm alignment of property requirements with business strategy
desc: Creating alignment between the requirement of properties and the overall business strategy. This process requires the organization to align the requirement of properties in accordance with its business strategies of the organization.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Appraise the external environment
desc: Evaluating the impact of the external environment. Evaluate the circumstances, objects, events, and aspects surrounding an organization that affects its actions and selections and that recognizes its opportunities and risks.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Determine build, buy, or lease decision
desc: Deciding whether to buy or build properties. Study the market forces about property prices and cost of construction in order to take decisions based on the market research.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Plan facility
desc: Recognizing the needs of facility users in order to construct a project proposal that meets those needs.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Design facility
desc: Preparing and analyzing different designs for a facility in order to finalize which design will be the most suitable option.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Analyze budget
desc: Evaluating the feasibility of budgets prepared for the construction of facilities.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Select property
desc: Assessing and choosing the appropriate property. Analyze the property requirements. Review the available property options. Finalize the most suitable option.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Negotiate terms for facility
desc: Discussing the terms and conditions of facilities to be occupied according to the business requirements and availability of budgets.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Manage construction or modification to building
desc: Constructing the buildings. Manage renovations according to requirements and demands.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Provide workspace and facilities
desc: Managing the provision of the workspace and its assets. Arrange an office space with all assets (tables, chairs, computers, admin staff, etc.) according to requirements.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Acquire workspace and facilities
desc: Attaining the office space with all assets (tables, chairs, computers, admin staff, etc.) according to requirements.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Change fit/form/function of workspace and facilities
desc: Modifying the formation of the workspace and its assets. Make necessary changes in an office space with all assets (tables, chairs, computers, admin staff, interior designing, etc.) according to requirements.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Manage facilities operations
desc: Managing all operational activities of the facility. Manage how each function/business unit works. Support the manufacturing facility to attain organizational goals.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Relocate people
desc: Shifting staff or employees from one place to another place according to changes in business requirements.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Relocate material and tools
desc: Relocating the tools and raw materials. Shift raw or finished material and machines of company from one place to another place according to changes in business requirements.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Provide facility access and security
desc: Ensuring safe, controlled access to organizational facilities by implementing and maintaining physical security protocols, systems, and procedures. This includes issuing and managing access credentials; monitoring entry points; coordinating visitor access; and operating security technologies such as surveillance, alarms, and access-control systems. Establish and enforce policies to protect employees, visitors, assets, and information; respond to security incidents or breaches; and routinely assess the effectiveness of security measures.
notes: Office leases and workspace across the three markets.

name: Design and construct assets
desc: Designing and constructing assets such as machines, tools, factories, etc. Manage steps to acquire assets including managing capital, as well as planning, scheduling, and overseeing acquisition/construction.

name: Manage capital program for assets
desc: Producing and maintaining a planning schedule and a financial plan to purchase or manufacture assets. Determine the investment plan, monitor capital, and secure the necessary financing in order to realize completion of the program.

name: Define capital investment plan
desc: Establishing what funds will be invested in the construction of assets for the advancement of established business objectives.

name: Monitor capital program
desc: Monitoring plans on capital projects. Capital projects can be purchasing buildings, lands, etc.

name: Secure construction financing
desc: Acquiring the loans needed to construct necessary assets.

name: Design and plan asset construction
desc: Outlining the steps and strategies needed to construct assets. Verify that all regulations are adhered to and that all permissions have been granted. Organize and plan for resources to complete construction.

name: Develop construction strategy
desc: Developing a strategy to perform asset construction. Assure that timelines, regulations, and resources are on task and on budget.

name: Perform construction performance management
desc: Managing the construction process to ensure that activates are on task, on budget, and are being performed with safety and quality in mind.

name: Obtain construction permissions
desc: Gathering the required permits for construction from the proper jurisdiction. This may include inspections during and after construction to verify that the new asset meets all national, regional, and local codes.

name: Design assets
desc: Designing assets to meet organizational needs as well as ensuring that the asset adheres to all national, regional, and local construction codes.

name: Plan construction resources
desc: Determining what resources will need to be acquired in order to carry out construction. Plan when, where, and how resources will be used. Determine the length of time resources will be utilized.

name: Schedule and perform construction work
desc: Arranging a timetable for which to perform construction work. Schedule resources to contract assets for new or replacement assets. Reschedule or redesign assets if needed.

name: Schedule construction work
desc: Defining a timetable for which to execute the construction of the asset.

name: Obtain resources
desc: Gathering resources needed to complete all construction work. Verify that all resources have the proper training and skills to perform the work.

name: Construct new assets
desc: Building new assets necessary for the organization. Be aware of any construction codes and permits that need to be addressed.

name: Augment existing assets
desc: Modifying existing assets to align with the changing needs of the organization. Be aware of any construction codes and permits that need to be addressed.

name: Renew/Replace assets
desc: Determining the need to replace existing assets. Be aware of any construction codes and permits that need to be addressed.

name: Manage asset construction
desc: Overseeing the performance and quality of work. Assure that records are maintained throughout the construction process. Adhere to all safety, security, and access regulations set forth by the organization and all government standards.

name: Monitor work performance
desc: Monitoring construction to insure that all regulatory laws are being adhered to, that all work is being performed in a timely manner, and that quality assurance is met at all steps of the construction process.

name: Undertake construction quality control
desc: Implementing a checks and balances system to verify that the construction was performed correctly. Rework when errors are found.

name: Create work and asset records
desc: Implementing records to include all construction work that has been performed. Include all new or modified construction, and any construction or regulatory issues that might have occurred.

name: Manage safety, security, and access to sites
desc: Ensuring that safety, security, and access is maintained. Provide a workplace that meets and exceeds all local, state, and federal guidelines. Provide security and access to the building site as set forth by safety and organizational guidelines.

name: Schedule and perform commissioning
desc: Scheduling and performing commissioning activities to verify that constructed assets operate as intended, meet specified requirements, and are ready for handover, use, or operational acceptance.

name: Maintain assets
desc: Preserving assets through the planning, managing, and performance of preventative, routine, and critical maintenance work.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Plan asset maintenance
desc: Ensuring that necessary resources are available and tasks are prioritized accordingly through planning. Provide strategies and policies that identify tasks that need to be completed, and the resources necessary to fulfill those tasks.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Develop maintenance strategies
desc: Creating goals and agendas to better realize the success of the maintenance policies that have been put into place.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Analyze assets and predict maintenance requirements
desc: Evaluating assets in order to project future requirements for maintenance. Evaluate the present working condition of assets. Determine the future maintenance requirements of assets.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Specify maintenance policies
desc: Communicating policies in regards to asset maintenance. Provide a clear set of procedures and policies that outline what will be involved in the maintenance process.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Integrate preventive maintenance into operations schedule
desc: Devising a methodology and procedure for assimilating the works of planned maintenance into the schedule scheme for the processing of finished products that utilizes the same machinery.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Identify work management tasks & priorities
desc: Identifying the steps needed for asset maintenance. List out the those tasks that are involved in completing this process. Prioritize the tasks that are created.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Conduct resource planning
desc: Analyzing workload needs in relation to asset maintenance and plan resources around those needs.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Create asset work plans
desc: Creating procedures on how to maintain assets.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Manage asset maintenance
desc: Ensuring that asset maintenance is conducted in a timely manner and successfully. Schedule work with the required resources with an eye on quality control and safety. Verify that contracted maintenance meets performance targets.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Schedule maintenance work
desc: Defining a timetable for which to execute the maintenance of the asset.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Obtain required resources
desc: Gathering resources needed to complete all maintenance work. Verify that all resources have the proper training and skills to perform the work.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Undertake quality control
desc: Implementing a checks and balances system to verify that the maintenance was performed correctly. Rework when errors are found.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Update work and asset records
desc: Modifying existing maintenance records to include all new work that has been performed, what assets were serviced, and any issues that might have arisen.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Manage maintenance work safety
desc: Assuring that all safety laws and regulations are being implemented and followed. Align practices with regulatory bureaus such as OSHA , EHS, and ISO.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Define maintenance performance targets
desc: Outlining what should be achieved through predictive indicators with regard to performing maintenance. This could include the length of time it takes to perform routine maintenance or how often unplanned maintenance feasibly occur.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Monitor maintenance performance against targets/contracts
desc: Following set performance targets, monitor and gage the success of the organization in meeting those targets.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Perform asset maintenance
desc: Engaging in all aspects of asset maintenance. Ensure that all assets are functioning properly and to all specified codes and regulations where applicable. Maintenance includes all preventative, routine, and corrective activates.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Perform preventative asset maintenance
desc: Performing prophylactic maintenance in an effort to avoid corrective or unplanned repairs.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Perform routine asset maintenance
desc: Carrying out required maintenance to continue upkeep of equipment or assets.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Perform corrective asset maintenance and repairs
desc: Repairing or correcting faults that occur with an asset. This could be a break or other repairable damage.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Identify unplanned maintenance requirements
desc: Realizing potential or current problems with assets that would require unplanned maintenance. Unplanned maintenance is a repair or change that needs to be made that is not preventative or routine.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Perform unplanned maintenance and repairs
desc: Performing repairs that occur outside of normal routine or preventative maintenance.
notes: Internal IT asset inventory and lifecycle.

name: Manage asset end-of-life
desc: Managing the disposition of assets at their end-of-life. End-of-life for an asset may be due to obsolescence, replacement, excess capacity, or disrepair among other potential factors. Steps may include decommissioning, disassembly, recycling, etc. Tracking and reporting may also be appropriate for some or all asset types due to law, regulation, or social/environmental responsibility.

name: Develop exit strategy
desc: Creating a strategy for managing asset exits.

name: Monitor useful life of assets
desc: Monitoring assets against their planned useful life. Each asset may have specific criteria that indicate their usability. This may include time-based, maintenance history, capacity planning, etc.

name: Perform cost vs. benefit analysis for replacement
desc: Cost/benefit analysis of assets to determine retention or end-of-life. Evaluating asset total lifecycle cost against other factors such as repair/refurbishment, replacement, and alternate solutions.

name: Decommission productive assets
desc: Retiring assets that are no longer viable to the business. Decommission assets that are no longer in working order, are out of date, or whose maintenance exceeds the cost of replacement.
notes: Secure decommission and data destruction - a real audit control.

name: Perform sale or trade
desc: Performing the sale of assets. Achieve and complete the sale process. Deliver the end product to the customers.

name: Manage take-back centers
