notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Develop training plan
desc: Creating a detailed summary of all the actions relevant to teaching a person a particular skill or type of behavior. Determine who will deliver the training. Determine when and where the apprentice or trainee needs to go to receive the structured component of the training.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Develop communication plan
desc: Developing a plan for imparting or exchanging information relevant the to change. Define goals, objectives, and audience. Gather tools for all communications.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Assign change champion(s)
desc: Utilizing champions that have been trained to carry out needed changes. Engage champions to communicate roles and responsibilities for the change.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Develop rewards/incentives plan
desc: Creating and designing the plan for rewarding the employees exhibiting the desired behavior. Specify rewards in recognition of service, effort, or achievement regarding the change, including bonuses, compensation, stock options, profit sharing, vacations, and flexible time.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Establish change adoption measures
desc: Establishing a system or standard of measurement for measuring the adoption of the change. Consider activities such as the number of people who have adopted the change, how quickly have they adopted, number of unique adopters, and adopters by teams/divisions.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Establish/Clarify new roles
desc: Establishing and explaining the new roles to employees. Assign roles and responsibilities to resources.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Identify budget/roles
desc: Creating a plan of financial outlay for the newly defined roles. Determine the amount of capital the organization is willing to invest in effectuating these new roles, how would the roles be financed, and what would comprise the ROI from these flows. Coordinate personnel responsible for change management and the finance division.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Implement change
desc: Effectuating the change within the desired impact areas of the organization. Ensure adequate commitment from all corners of the organization for the desired change. Create support structures. Refashion all processes deemed necessary. Observe the progress.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Create commitment for improvement/change
desc: Kindling an organization wide commitment for effectuating the change. Effectively communicate the advantages of the desired change. Personalize the pitch for change.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Reengineer business processes and systems
desc: Restructuring, redesigning, repurposing, and/or retrofitting existing business processes, activities, and frameworks in order to effectuate the desired change. Review pertinent processes from the ground up by starting with the desired result. (Build on Select a process improvement methodology [11138] to create business processes that perfectly fit with the road map for change.)
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Support transition to new roles or exit strategies for incumbents
desc: Supporting the transition of personnel to new roles and the dismissal of any existing employees, necessitated for the desired change. Create an on-boarding process for seamlessly transitioning personnel to new roles. Offer orientation and training. Address any concerns. Create a structured procedure for the discharge of incumbents from their positions.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Monitor change
desc: Monitoring activities in the change process in order to assess the performance of individual agents and the process as a whole. Oversee the implementation of activities needed for effectuating the change. Track the pace, impact, enthusiasm, reaction, and feedback over the change process.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Report on change
desc: Reporting on the outcome of the change. Document changes and the impact those changes had on critical assets. Share findings with those within the target audience: those impacted by the change, change champions, stakeholders, etc.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Sustain improvement
desc: Sustaining the impact of the change process in order to enact continual process improvement. Monitor the performance of re-engineered business processes. Identify best practices and potential issues. Effectuate remedial steps.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Monitor improved process performance
desc: Monitoring the performance of improved business processes. Track the key performance indicators of the upgraded processes in order to gauge its contribution to the desired change. Expedite through the use of business process management software.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Capture and reuse lessons learned from change process
desc: Documenting and standardizing insights gleaned and the knowledge acquired from studying the change process already implemented. Create case studies/best practices guides from the process of implementing change. Include experienced personnel.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Take corrective action as necessary
desc: Implement corrective action to adjust the re-engineered processes for maximizing the desired impact. Adjust business processes and systems to implement the desired change.
notes: Change management for the EOS transition and system migrations.

name: Develop and manage enterprise-wide knowledge management (KM) capability
desc: Creating and administering the capability of the organization's knowledge management function. Develop a strategy for knowledge management. Assess capabilities of the knowledge management function.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop KM strategy
desc: Creating a plan for managing the organization's knowledge base. Determine what kind of specialized knowledge the organization possesses, which elements of this collective knowledge can prove beneficial, how to capture and maintain this knowledge, how to grant access to this library of information, and how the organization should proceed.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop governance model with roles and accountability
desc: Developing a structure for the governance of the organization's collective knowledge. Gather, maintain, and make accessible the collective knowledge base. Develop a standard procedure for the conservation and perpetuation of the organization's knowledge. Create policies for the usage and maintenance of this knowledge. Establish specialized roles.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Define roles and accountability of core group versus operating units
desc: Clearly determining the roles and responsibilities of all personnel involved in the management of the organization's corpus of knowledge. Flesh out the roles and responsibilities of the KM core group, as well as the operational staff involved in the upkeep of the knowledge management program.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop funding models
desc: Analyze the organization's current approach to funding. Learn from the funding approaches of peer organizations. Evaluate the revenue potential and costs of those short-list funding models. Select funding models to implement.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Identify links to key initiatives
desc: Identifying any links that exist between the strategy for knowledge management and any other functional areas. Determine any correlations that exist between the strategic road map for the knowledge management and any other functional areas. Study each function's/unit's attributes.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop core KM methodologies
desc: Creating core knowledge management procedures and methodologies. Initiate developing a strategy, planning, execution, and improvement.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Assess IT needs and engage IT function
desc: Determining the IT needs for developing the knowledge management strategy, and collaborating with the IT function to implement the strategy. Assess requirements for technologies such as computer hardware, software, electronics, semiconductors, internet, and telecommunications equipment in order to effectively build and implement the strategy for knowledge management.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop training and communication plans
desc: Creating plans for KM training plans and conveying the knowledge management strategy within the organization. Create training programs, sessions, and activities in order to familiarize employees and management with the concept of knowledge management.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop change management approaches
desc: Creating approaches for effectively administering the changes in knowledge management. Design an approach that transforms individuals, teams, and the organization to a desired future state represented by the change.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop strategic measures and indicators
desc: Establishing measures and indicators for evaluating the performance of the knowledge management function. Define key performance indicators such as the amount of knowledge assets created and number of knowledge projects undertaken.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Assess KM capabilities
desc: Assessing the maturity of the existing initiatives in knowledge management, and evaluating existing KM approaches. Identify the gaps and needs in order to enhance the existing KM approaches. Develop and implement new KM approaches.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Assess maturity of existing KM initiatives
desc: Evaluating if initiatives are effective or should be discarded. Design a framework for assessing maturity, typically from Level 1 (undefined), Level 2 (repeatable), Level 3 (defined), and Level 4 (managed) through Level 5 (optimized).
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Evaluate existing KM approaches
desc: Evaluating existing procedures, policies, and guidelines for knowledge management. Study and examine the organization's approach against industry best practices by benchmarking, competitive analysis, etc.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Identify gaps and needs
desc: Assessing the KM approach evaluations in order to identify any gaps or needs. Compare the performance of the KM approach against the desired or expected performance, as well as against the standard knowledge management industry approach.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Design and implement KM capabilities
desc: Creating knowledge bases and other repositories to preserve and develop company expertise, and to train new employees.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop new KM approaches
desc: Designing new policies, procedures, and guidelines to support knowledge management.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Design resource model for KM approaches
desc: Creating a model to describe resources and approaches to organization's knowledge management. Establish standards and guidelines to be followed.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Implement new KM approaches
desc: Implementing new policies, procedures, and guidelines to support knowledge management.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Leverage and enhance IT for KM approaches
desc: Using existing technologies to improve organization's knowledge management processes. Research available third-party offerings. Develop proprietary solutions. Employ knowledge engineers, data scientists and other relevant personnel.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Develop measures
desc: Creating metrics that can be used to systematically describe KM approaches and capabilities. Choose applicable scales, benchmarks and units of measure. Determine required precision and error rates.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Evolve and sustain KM capabilities
desc: Developing resources for improved knowledge management and knowledge engineering.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Enhance/Modify existing KM approaches
desc: Leveraging KM evaluations and identified gap to enhance existing approaches.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Sustain awareness and engagement
desc: Developing awareness about available knowledge bases and promoting their use to maximize their impact.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Expand KM infrastructure to meet demand
desc: Augmenting available resources to better leverage the offerings of the organization to serve existing clients and to expand the client base.
notes: Knowledge base maturity is the lever on service desk efficiency.

name: Manage Content
desc: Storing, managing, curating and delivering enterprise content and knowledge assets to enable consistent reuse and informed decision making.  Establish structures and governance that support classification, semantic enrichment, and lifecycle management of content across formats and repositories.  This includes all forms of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning assisted tagging, automated classification, and semantic content processing.

name: Define content management strategy
desc: Establishing a foundational plan that guides how an organization manages its content through the content lifecycle. Outlining the strategy for organizing, delivering, and facilitating access to enterprise content.

name: Establish content management objectives
desc: Establishing objectives for content management that enhance the organization and accessibility of enterprise content. Objectives can include curation, findability, consistency, user-centric design, lifecycle management, governance and roles, quality assurance, and measurement and evaluation.

name: Develop content management governance model
desc: Establishing a structured framework with roles and responsibilities to oversee and guide content management practices within an organization to ensure content is managed consistently, remains high-quality, meets the needs of users, and enhances the overall content management strategy.

name: Develop content management funding models
desc: Defining funding approaches for content management activities, capabilities, and infrastructure to support sustainable operations, investment prioritization, and alignment with organizational objectives.

name: Develop core content management methodologies
desc: Identifying and implementing content management methodologies to effectively store, deliver, and facilitate access to enterprise content. Core methodologies may include prioritization of critical or high-value content, findability to ensure ease of locating relevant content, content lifecycle management, standardization of content creation, review and access, collaboration, and technology integration.

name: Assess content management IT needs and engage IT function
desc: Assessing technology requirements for content management and collaborating with the IT function to align systems, integration, security, and support with content management needs. This includes leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI).

name: Develop content management training and communication plans
desc: Developing training, change and communication plans to support the organization's content management practices. Define target audiences, required competencies, learning objectives, and delivery methods to ensure consistent understanding and adoption of content standards, tools, and workflows. Create communication strategies to promote awareness of content governance, reinforce expectations, and inform stakeholders of process updates, system changes, and best practices. Coordinate with internal partners to design training materials, schedule learning sessions, and disseminate communications that enable effective and compliant content creation, storage, use, and lifecycle management. Monitor participation, evaluate effectiveness, and continuously improve based on feedback and evolving organizational needs.

name: Develop strategic measures and indicators for content management
desc: Defining and implementing performance measures to assess the effectiveness and strategic value of content management practices. Align indicators with organizational goals, governance requirements, and user needs. Specify data sources, measurement methods, and reporting cadences to provide reliable insight into content quality, accessibility, utilization, and lifecycle compliance. Collaborate with stakeholders to validate metric definitions, integrate measures into dashboards, and set expectations for monitoring and improvement. Periodically review and refine measures in response to changing priorities and requirements.

name: Manage content intelligence and insights
desc: Monitor and analyze content ecosystem performance to understand search behavior, user intent, knowledge gaps, content effectiveness, and content lifecycle health. Use content usage patterns and derived insights to identify emerging needs, anticipate gaps, recommend updates or new content, and continuously optimize the relevance, quality, and accessibility of the content ecosystem. This includes leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI)

name: Develop and manage taxonomies
desc: Developing and managing taxonomies, ontologies, and related semantic structures to classify, enrich, and relate enterprise content and knowledge assets, supporting consistent interpretation, discoverability, reuse, and advanced capabilities such as automated classification and semantic processing.

name: Determine content management requirements
desc: Identifying functional, operational, governance, and compliance requirements that content management practices and solutions must satisfy across the organization.

name: Define content taxonomies
desc: Establishing content metadata structures that function as a common classification language by defining hierarchical categories and attributes used to organize and relate content, ensuring consistency across formats, business areas, and locations and supporting discoverability and semantic enrichment.

name: Define file naming standards and tagging requirements
desc: Defining standardized conventions for naming, versioning, and tagging digital files and content assets to support consistency, findability, and compliance across the organization. Establish required metadata elements and tagging structures aligned with enterprise taxonomies, information architecture, and regulatory or operational needs.

name: Define content systems of record and storage requirements
desc: Defining requirements for systems of record and storage locations to ensure content is securely stored, retrievable, retained appropriately, and aligned with governance and compliance needs.

name: Define content access controls
desc: Defining rules and permissions that govern who can create, view, modify, and distribute content to protect sensitive information and support appropriate access.

name: Develop content audit and retention requirements
desc: Establishing audit and retention requirements to ensure content is reviewed, retained, archived, or disposed of in accordance with governance, legal, and operational obligations.

name: Manage content infrastructure
desc: Managing the systems, tools, and repositories that support content storage, access, administration, and control across the content lifecycle. Consider AI supported content services (e.g., auto classification, semantic enrichment, embeddings stores, and knowledge graph infrastructure).

name: Set up and maintain systems of record and storage locations
desc: Establishing and maintaining content repositories and systems of record to support secure storage, organization, access, and lifecycle management.

name: Implement and execute content administration responsibilities
desc: Executing administrative activities required to manage content systems, permissions, structures, and configurations in accordance with defined standards and governance.

name: Audit content compliance
desc: Overseeing activities to verify that content complies with established standards, policies, and requirements across its lifecycle.

name: Plan content audits
desc: Planning content audits by defining scope, criteria, timing, and responsibilities to assess compliance and effectiveness of content management practices.

name: Perform content audits
desc: Conducting reviews of content to evaluate compliance with defined standards, controls, and retention requirements. Includes auditing for semantic accuracy, metadata completeness, and AI-readiness. Consider leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI).

name: Track content non-compliance resolution
desc: Tracking identified content non-compliance issues and monitoring corrective actions to ensure timely resolution and adherence to content standards.

name: Develop and manage content
desc: Creating, acquiring, refining, and maintaining content to ensure it is accurate, relevant, consistent, and aligned with organizational standards and intended use. This includes leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI). Apply metadata, tags, and semantic relationships to improve findability, compliance, and reuse.

name: Identify new and existing content
desc: Identifying content needs and existing content assets to support reuse, updates, and alignment with organizational requirements.

name: Identify content control requirements
desc: Identifying control requirements for content, including review, approval, access, and compliance needs across the content lifecycle.

name: Prepare created content
desc: Preparing newly created content for use by applying required standards, structure, and controls prior to review and approval.

name: Prepare acquired content
desc: Preparing externally sourced or acquired content for organizational use by validating quality, applying standards, and aligning it with governance requirements.

name: Refine content
desc: Refining content to improve clarity, accuracy, consistency, and quality for its existing intended purpose and audience. This includes leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI).

name: Enhance and adapt content
desc: Enhancing and adapting content to support new or different audiences, formats, channels, or contexts while preserving core meaning and intent of the original content. This includes leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI).

name: Perform content branding
desc: Applying branding elements and standards to content to ensure consistent identity, presentation, and alignment with organizational guidelines.

name: Execute technical edits on content
desc: Performing technical edits to ensure content meets formatting, accessibility, usability, and technical quality requirements. This includes leveraging all forms of new and evolving technology such as artificial intelligence (AI).

name: Deliver approved content
desc: Delivering approved content to intended audiences through appropriate channels, repositories, or platforms in accordance with defined standards and controls.

name: Assess and approve content
desc: Reviewing content to confirm accuracy, quality, compliance, and readiness prior to approval for distribution or use.

name: Publish approved content
desc: Publishing approved content to designated locations or channels to make it available to intended users.

name: Store approved content
desc: Storing approved content in designated repositories to support controlled access, retrieval, and lifecycle management.

name: Control delivered content
desc: Controlling the use, evaluation, retention, and disposition of delivered content to ensure continued relevance, compliance, and value over time. Includes monitoring content quality and semantic coherence.

name: Evaluate content
desc: Evaluating content usage, effectiveness, and relevance to inform updates, improvements, or retirement decisions.

name: Archive content
desc: Archiving content that is no longer actively used but must be retained to meet governance, legal, or historical requirements.

name: Delete content
desc: Deleting content that has reached the end of its retention period and is no longer required, in accordance with defined policies and controls.

name: Measure and benchmark
desc: Defining and managing measurement and benchmarking. Measure and benchmark the performance of internal processes, as well as the organization as a whole.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Define and manage organizational performance strategy
desc: Creating and implementing a strategy for managing organizational performance. The strategy should include approaches for measuring, tracking, streamlining, and improving internal performance. It encompasses a blueprint for the tactical measurement of internal processes and work force improvement, in alignment with Employee Metrics Developed and Managed [10526].
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Define enterprise measurement models
desc: Developing a model for organization's management systems. Develop a high-level measurement system to track performance across the enterprise or in specific functions or business units. Determine which processes to measure, which measures to use, how often to measure, and measurement targets. Review strategic decisions about how to best measure an organization.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Maintain enterprise measurement models
desc: Reviewing, evaluating, and updating enterprise measurement models. Align measurement models to current and future goals and performance targets, and make adjustments to support visibility and reporting needs across the organization.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Benchmark performance
desc: Comparing organizational performance internally or externally with other organizations.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Conduct performance assessments
desc: Measuring, researching, and recording the performance of people, processes, mechanisms, or other areas of the business that the organization wants to benchmark or track.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Develop benchmarking capabilities
desc: Improving an organization's ability to compare its performance internally or externally, and maintaining benchmarking relationships with other organizations. Train staff in benchmarking. Develop technological solutions or other materials to aid benchmarking efforts. Consult with external entities to gain knowledge or tools to help benchmark.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Conduct internal and external benchmarking
desc: Benchmarking internal processes and against external competitors.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Conduct gap analysis
desc: Examining performance against benchmarked organizations or entities. Determine how much performance needs to change to meet expectations. Reach strategic goals.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Establish need for change
desc: Establishing a need for changing the performance of the organization. Make use of the gap analysis results in order to define the need for change.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Evaluate performance
desc: Assessing process data, measures, and trends in an effort to evaluate process performance and identify possible improvements.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Establish performance indicators (measures)
desc: Designing key measures that analyze and interpret how effectively the business is achieving its objectives.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Establish monitoring frequency
desc: Deciding on the appropriate amount of supervisions that are needed to effectively assess the performance of business plans.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Collect performance data
desc: Consolidating acquired metrics and trends. Provide data that can be benchmarked against historical data.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Calculate performance measures
desc: Measuring the performance of process planning. Quantify the performance, record results of the performance tests, and report them to the appropriate authority.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Identify performance trends
desc: Recognizing the trends in performance. Carefully and strategically assess the results in order to effectively spot the trends.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Analyze performance
desc: Evaluating the gaps between achieved and benchmarked performance. Analyze how performance differs from the optimal or expected performance.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Prepare performance reports
desc: Creating reports that systematically record and represent the performance planning. Construct a detailed report specifying the performance, and include indicators such as the performance gaps, performance trends, and analysis.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Develop performance improvement plan
desc: Using performance indicators to report, analyze, and create a detailed performance improvement plan to bridge the performance gaps.
notes: EOS scorecard, MSP benchmarks and the measurement layer over everything else.

name: Develop, Manage, and Deliver Analytics
desc: Creating new and improving existing analytical capabilities to enhance data management pipeline.

name: Identify needs from stakeholders
desc: Gathering information from stakeholders prior to conducting analytics.

name: Scope analytics project
desc: Determining the size and scale of the project based upon the collected information and analytics.

name: Develop and manage hypotheses
desc: Creating theories that explain empirical data. Use the hypotheses to guide feature selection in the process of data collection.

name: Collect data
desc: Gathering and harvesting structured and unstructured data from disparate sources. Clean and pre-process data. Remove duplicates. Convert to a uniform format to make records comparable.

name: Prepare data
desc: Creation and validation of data in order to initiate the process of analysis.

name: Analyze data
desc: Conducting data analysis. Choose statistical algorithms that best reveal patterns and trends in the data. Compare with hypotheses and time series forecasts. Determine error rates and significant outliers.

name: Create data models
desc: Creation of conceptual and physical data models as an outline for data structure and storage.

name: Review data models with stakeholders
desc: Confirm data models represent the hypothesis supporting the original research question

name: Refine data models
desc: Make required changes to data model based upon review with stakeholders.

name: Report on analysis
desc: Summarizing and documenting the results of data analysis. Create graphs and visualizations to illustrate numerical findings to make them more accessible to readers.

name: Identify remedial actions
desc: Determining the steps that need to be taken to correct the shortcomings.

name: Manage Environmental Health and Safety (EHS)
desc: Determining the impacts of environmental health and safety. Create and implement the EHS program. Train and educate employees of the EHS function. Oversee and manage the EHS program.

name: Determine environmental health and safety impacts
desc: Determining the impact of EHS offering--and the procedures it employs to process them--on the environment at large, as well as the health and safety of employees. Evaluate the environmental impact of the organization's products, services, and operations. Conduct health, safety, and environmental audits.

name: Evaluate environmental impact of products, services, and operations
desc: Evaluating the impact of offerings and the auxiliary operations required to process them on the immediate ecosystem and the environment at large. Study the lifecycle of the products/services offered by the organization. Estimate any affect on the environment through metrics such as a calculation of carbon footprint.

name: Conduct health and safety and environmental audits
desc: Conducting an inspection to verify that the organization adequately complies with the environmental, health, and safety standards. Audit procedures and records regarding responsibility for the environment, health, and safety.

name: Develop EHS program
desc: Identify the requirements for regulation and shareholders. Assess future risks and opportunities. Develop a policy for the EHS program. Record and manage EHS program events.

name: Identify regulatory and stakeholder requirements
desc: Determining any protocols or standards to comply with, set by regulatory agencies or the organization's stakeholders. Closely examine all standards and matters of compliance relating to the environment, health, and safety.

name: Assess future risks and opportunities
desc: Evaluating any risks and opportunities that might affect the environmental, health, and safety of products/services. Leverage techniques such as cost-benefit analysis, trend extrapolation, systems analysis, social surveys, historical surveys, historical analogy, Delphi, conferences, workshops, briefings, hearings, advisory committees, moot courts, artistic judgment, on-site field investigation, scaling techniques, and scenario creation.

name: Create EHS policy
desc: Creating a plan for managing the environmental, health, and safety impact of products/services. Establish minimum requirements for the organization regarding the environment at large and the health and safety of employees. Develop policies, written procedures, and supporting tools to dictate how the organization will meet policy requirements.

name: Record and manage EHS events
desc: Recording and managing all events and activities associated with complying with environmental, health and safety standards. Create event calendars. Assign funds. Educate employees. Conduct events.

name: Monitor and manage EHS program
desc: Managing the performance, costs and benefits of EHS. Measure and report the performance of EHS. Implement plans for emergency response and pollution prevention. Train and educate employees. Provide EHS support.

name: Manage EHS costs and benefits
desc: Administering the costs and benefits of EHS management program. Evaluate program costs to ensure that the benefits of the program always outweigh its costs.

name: Measure and report EHS performance
desc: Using performance techniques and indicators. Utilize number of audits or inspections performed, safety committee meetings, the number and types of findings and observations, timely preventive maintenance tasks performed, etc.

name: Implement emergency response program
desc: Implementing a program for organizing, coordinating, and directing available resources to respond to the event. Conduct a risk assessment to identify potential emergency scenarios in order to create a program that ensures that resources are on hand--or quickly available--in case of emergencies.

name: Implement pollution prevention program
desc: Implementing a program that reduces or eliminates the creation of pollutants through increased efficiency in the use of raw materials, energy, water, or other resources. Implement a program to inspect facilities that store, manufacture, or use hazardous, toxic, or polluting materials.

name: Train and educate functional employees
desc: Conducting programs such as on-the-job training sessions, group training workshops, and online training.

name: Provide EHS support
desc: Supporting employees in light of the organization's environmental, health, and safety policies and standards. Provide medical insurance, maternity leave, environmental education, training over safety, etc.

name: Manage sustainability
desc: Developing and managing sustainability practices for the organization. Ensure proper understanding and communication of ESG standards, requirements, capabilities, and future trends. Promote awareness, alignment, and continuity.

name: Develop sustainability capability
desc: Developing sustainability (ESG) capabilities for the organization. Understand and communicate legal, regulatory, and social/environmental requirements. Establish policies, objectives, guidelines and approaches for ESG efforts and reporting.

name: Identify sustainability requirements
desc: Identifying, documenting, and communicating sustainability requirements. Closely examine all standards and matters of compliance relating to ESG. Determine protocols or standards to comply with, set by regulatory agencies or the organizations stakeholders.

name: Define sustainability disclosure requirements
desc: Defining and communicating sustainability disclosure requirements. Clarify and align disclosure requirements to other organizational reporting requirements and needs. Integrate preparation and reporting activities.

name: Define sustainability governance requirements
desc: Defining governance requirements for sustainability. Include structure, roles, alignment to organization models, processes and standards to be applied.

name: Define sustainability functional and performance requirements
desc: Defining functional and performance requirements for sustainability. Align with ESG strategies, goals, and the implementation of sustainability efforts across the organization, provide a roadmap and visibility to shared and collective requirements.

name: Establish sustainability goals/objectives
desc: Establishing organizational sustainability goals/objectives. Gather, align, and promote organization-wide sustainability goals that collectively address the overall sustainability requirements. Ensure the goals are measurable and have qualitative and quantitative targets.

name: Create sustainability policies
desc: Establishing, documenting, and communicating sustainability policies. Develop policies, written procedures, and supporting tools to dictate how the organization will meet policy requirements.

name: Define sustainability measures
desc: Defining sustainability measures. Provide organization-wide measures, to include data collection strategies, calculations, analytics, and reporting formats.

name: Create sustainability plan(s)
desc: Creating sustainability plans. Develop and socialize sustainability plans for the organization, functional units, and support services. Ensure alignment to sustainability requirements, goals, and governance.

name: Manage sustainability capability
desc: Managing sustainability across the organization. Provide training, support, reporting, and oversight to the distributed sustainability efforts across functional units and support services.

name: Provide sustainability training
desc: Providing sustainability training and awareness. Plan, prepare, and oversee delivery of sustainability education and enablement activities.

name: Provide sustainability support
desc: Providing support for sustainability activities. Augment functional units and support teams with coaching, mentoring, and SME capacity to perform sustainability projects and activities.

name: Perform sustainability reporting
desc: Conducting and supporting sustainability reporting. Collect, analyze, and report sustainability performance to requirements. Align reporting across functional units and support teams.

name: Measure sustainability performance
desc: Measuring sustainability performance. Setup, collect, and validate sustainability data. Conduct audits and inspections. Evaluate results to requirements and targets. Identify and track resolution of gaps and variances.

name: Prepare sustainability statements
desc: Preparing sustainability statements. Given the multitude of potential audiences for reporting, alignment and consistency of sustainability statements provides clarity and reusability for those audiences.
